[backend]       version: "1.0.0"
[backend]       domain: sre
[backend]       tags: [data-access, protocol, shared]
[backend]     ---
[backend]     
[backend]     # Data Access Protocol
[backend]     
[backend]     ## Tool Invocation Discipline
[backend]     
[backend]     When calling any data tool (`get_metrics`, `get_logs`, `get_service_health`,
[backend]     `get_deployments`, `query_db`), you MUST pass the canonical service name as
[backend]     the `service` argument.
[backend]     
[backend]     **Rule**: Use the **exact** service identifier from the incident description
[backend]     verbatim (e.g. `"payment-service"`). Do not omit the `service` argument, do
[backend]     not paraphrase the name, and do not substitute a generic placeholder.
[backend]     
[backend]     **Why this matters**: Omitting or misspelling the service name causes tools
[backend]     to return an error — there is no default fallback. Agents will see
[backend]     `"error": "required parameter 'service' is missing"` if the argument is
[backend]     absent. Cross-agent correlation fails when different agents query different
[backend]     service names for the same incident.
[backend]     
[backend]     ## Correct Pattern
[backend]     
[backend]     ```
[backend]     get_metrics(service="payment-service")   # ✓ exact canonical name
[backend]     get_logs(service="payment-service")      # ✓ same canonical name
[backend]     get_deployments(service="payment-service")  # ✓ consistent
[backend]     ```
[backend]     
[backend]     ## Incorrect Patterns
[backend]     
[backend]     ```
[backend]     get_metrics()                   # ✗ missing service arg → tool returns error
[backend]     get_metrics(service="payment")  # ✗ partial name → tool returns error
[backend]     get_metrics(service="service")  # ✗ generic placeholder → tool returns error
[backend]     ```
[backend]     
[backend]     ## Where to Find the Canonical Name
[backend]     
[backend]     The canonical service name appears in:
[backend]     - The incident fixture: `spec.params.incident_fixture` → `services:` keys
[backend]     - The SRE's initial incident description passed to you at delegation time
[backend]     - The incident summary in your system context
[backend]     
[backend]     Use it verbatim. Do not normalise underscores to hyphens or vice versa unless
[backend]     the fixture explicitly lists both as aliases.
[backend]

[backend]     ---
[backend]     name: uncertainty-protocol
[backend]     description: >
[backend]       Structured gap-check and confidence-scoring protocol for analyst agents.
[backend]       Use this before writing any conclusion or hypothesis to ensure every claim
[backend]       is backed by evidence and gaps are explicitly declared rather than filled
[backend]       by speculation.
[backend]     metadata:
[backend]       version: "1.0.0"
[backend]       domain: sre
[backend]       tags: [uncertainty, protocol, shared]
[backend]     ---
[backend]     
[backend]     # Uncertainty Protocol — Telemetry Analyst
[backend]     
[backend]     Before writing any conclusion or hypothesis, complete the following block exactly.
[backend]     Do not skip it even if you believe the answer is obvious.
[backend]     
[backend]     ## Required Gap-Check Block
[backend]     
[backend]     After completing all tool calls for a question, produce:
[backend]     
[backend]     ```
[backend]     EVIDENCE_ACCESSED:
[backend]       - <tool_name>(<params>) → <key result in one line>
[backend]       - ... (one line per call made this turn)
[backend]     
[backend]     GAPS:
[backend]       - <question you cannot answer from the above results>
[backend]       - ... (empty list = [] if nothing is missing)
[backend]     
[backend]     CONFIDENCE: <0.0–1.0>
[backend]       Rule: must be ≤ 0.5 if GAPS is non-empty.
[backend]       Rule: must cite at least one EVIDENCE_ACCESSED entry to justify values > 0.7.
[backend]     ```
[backend]     
[backend]     ## When GAPS is non-empty
[backend]     
[backend]     Do **not** proceed to a conclusion. Instead write:
[backend]     
[backend]     ```
[backend]     CLARIFICATION_NEEDED: <the single most important missing piece>
[backend]     SUGGESTED_SOURCE: <which agent or tool could provide it>
[backend]     ```
[backend]     
[backend]     Do not fabricate an answer to fill the gap. A stated gap is more useful
[backend]     than a confident wrong conclusion.
[backend]     
[backend]     ## Telemetry-specific scope limits
[backend]     
[backend]     These questions are outside the telemetry agent's tool set. If asked about them,
[backend]     list them in GAPS and suggest the appropriate agent:
[backend]     
[backend]     | Question | Correct agent |
[backend]     |----------|---------------|
[backend]     | Root cause of DB connection pool saturation | DB Specialist |
[backend]     | Whether a deployment is responsible | Backend Engineer |
[backend]     | Whether a rollback is safe | Backend Engineer + Verifier |
[backend]     | Business impact in revenue terms | Comms Agent |
[backend]     
[backend]     ## Reporting Format
[backend]     
[backend]     Every conclusion must follow: **Observed → Evidence → Limitation**
[backend]     
[backend]     ```
[backend]     OBSERVED:   error_rate on payment-service = 23.2% (from get_metrics)
[backend]     EVIDENCE:   get_metrics("payment-service", metric="error_rate", window="15m") → 0.232
[backend]     LIMITATION: cannot determine if deployment at 09:55 is causal without backend data
[backend]     ```
[backend]

[backend]       Structured episodic memory protocol for agents operating in a multi-agent

[backend]     # Memory Protocol
[backend]     
[backend]     All agents share an episodic store. Unstructured writes cannot be reliably
[backend]     retrieved downstream. Use this format for every write.
[backend]     
[backend]     ## Write format — Evidence Card
[backend]     
[backend]     Every time you write to memory, produce exactly one card per finding:
[backend]     
[backend]     ```
[backend]     MEMORY_WRITE:
[backend]       service:       <service name, e.g. payment-service>
[backend]       metric:        <what was measured, e.g. p99_latency_ms>
[backend]       value:         <observed value or range, e.g. 4200>
[backend]       timestamp:     <ISO-8601 or "from run_id=<id>">
[backend]       source_agent:  <your agent name>
[backend]       tool_call:     <tool_name(params) that produced this value>
[backend]       interpretation: <one-sentence meaning, e.g. "exceeds 2 000 ms SLO">
[backend]     ```
[backend]     
[backend]     Write multiple cards if a single tool call yields multiple distinct facts.
[backend]     Do not combine unrelated facts in one card.
[backend]     
[backend]     ## Read format — Structured Query
[backend]     
[backend]     Before calling a tool that another agent may already have run, query memory:
[backend]     
[backend]     ```
[backend]     MEMORY_READ:
[backend]       service: <service name>
[backend]       metric:  <metric name>
[backend]     ```
[backend]     
[backend]     If the store returns a match, use it and note:
[backend]     
[backend]     ```
[backend]     RECALLED: <service>/<metric> = <value> (from <source_agent>)
[backend]     ```
[backend]     
[backend]     Do not re-run the same tool call if a valid recall exists.
[backend]     
[backend]     ## What not to write
[backend]     
[backend]     - Do not write summaries or prose paragraphs to memory.
[backend]     - Do not write hypotheses or confidence scores.
[backend]     - Do not write tool errors (write `GAPS` in the uncertainty block instead).

[backend]     - Severity classification decisions and the evidence that triggered them

[sre]     ---
[sre]     name: triage-protocol
[sre]     description: >
[sre]       Step-by-step incident triage protocol for the SRE orchestrator. Use this
[sre]       to guide parallel investigation dispatch, root-cause synthesis, mandatory
[sre]       verification gate, and final report. Applies to any SEV1/SEV2/SEV3 incident.
[sre]     metadata:
[sre]       version: "1.0.0"
[sre]       domain: sre
[sre]       tags: [triage, protocol, orchestrator]
[sre]     ---
[sre]     
[sre]     # Incident Triage Protocol
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 1 — Initial Assessment (< 2 minutes)
[sre]     - Confirm incident symptoms (latency, error rates, conversion impact).
[sre]     - Check if this is a new event or regression from a known issue.
[sre]     - Set initial severity (SEV1 / SEV2 / SEV3) based on customer impact.
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 2 — Parallel Investigation Delegation
[sre]     Immediately dispatch tasks to specialist agents:
[sre]     - **Telemetry Agent**: analyse span/trace latency breakdown, error rates, anomaly correlation.
[sre]     - **Backend Agent**: check recent deployments, connection pool usage, config changes.
[sre]     - **DB Agent**: inspect slow queries, lock contention, connection pool saturation.
[sre]     - **Comms Agent**: draft initial status-page update and internal War Room message.
[sre]     
[sre]     Do NOT wait for one agent to finish before calling the next. Dispatch all in sequence.
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 3 — Collect Findings
[sre]     Wait for each specialist to return a result, then aggregate.
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 4 — Root Cause & Action Plan
[sre]     Based on collected evidence, identify the most likely root cause and write:
[sre]     - Confirmed or suspected root cause
[sre]     - Immediate mitigation (rollback / feature flag / query kill)
[sre]     - Follow-up actions (monitoring, postmortem)
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 5 — Verification Gate (MANDATORY before any remediation action)
[sre]     Before calling `run_action`, you MUST delegate to the Verifier agent:
[sre]     - Call `delegate_to_verifier` with your root cause summary and action plan.
[sre]     - Wait for the Verifier response. It will contain one of:
[sre]       - `VERIFICATION: APPROVED` — proceed to Step 6

[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 7 — Remediation Action
[sre]     Only after receiving `VERIFICATION: APPROVED`, call `run_action` with the approved plan.

[sre]     # Memory Protocol
[sre]     
[sre]     All agents share an episodic store. Unstructured writes cannot be reliably
[sre]     retrieved downstream. Use this format for every write.
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Write format — Evidence Card
[sre]     
[sre]     Every time you write to memory, produce exactly one card per finding:
[sre]     
[sre]     ```
[sre]     MEMORY_WRITE:
[sre]       service:       <service name, e.g. payment-service>
[sre]       metric:        <what was measured, e.g. p99_latency_ms>
[sre]       value:         <observed value or range, e.g. 4200>
[sre]       timestamp:     <ISO-8601 or "from run_id=<id>">
[sre]       source_agent:  <your agent name>
[sre]       tool_call:     <tool_name(params) that produced this value>
[sre]       interpretation: <one-sentence meaning, e.g. "exceeds 2 000 ms SLO">
[sre]     ```
[sre]

[sre]

[db]     ---
[db]     name: lock-detection
[db]     description: >
[db]       Lock contention and deadlock analysis for database incidents. Use this
[db]       when observing lock_wait_timeout errors, sudden write queue buildup, or
[db]       P99 spikes on INSERT/UPDATE operations. Covers safe mitigations, risk
[db]       table, and blocking query kill procedure.
[db]     metadata:
[db]       version: "1.0.0"
[db]       domain: sre
[db]       tags: [locks, deadlocks, database, db]
[db]     ---
[db]     
[db]     # Lock Detection & Deadlock Analysis
[db]     
[db]     ## Symptoms
[db]     
[db]     - `lock_wait_timeout` errors in application logs.
[db]     - Sudden queue buildup on write operations.
[db]     - P99 spike on `INSERT`/`UPDATE` to `payments` or `transactions` table.
[db]     
[db]     ## Investigation Steps
[db]     
[db]     1. Call `get_metrics(service="{db_service}", metric="lock_wait_count", window="15m")`.
[db]     2. Call `get_metrics(service="{db_service}", metric="deadlock_count", window="15m")`.
[db]     3. Call `query_db(service="{db_service}", query_type="blocking_queries")` to get live pg_stat_activity data.
[db]     4. Call `query_db(service="{db_service}", query_type="pg_stat_activity")` for full connection picture.
[db]     5. Call `get_logs(service="{db_service}", level="ERROR", limit=10)` for lock timeout messages.
[db]     
[db]     ## Interpreting Results
[db]     
[db]     - `lock_wait_count > 50/min` → active lock contention.
[db]     - `deadlock_count > 0` → circular lock dependency, check transaction order in code.
[db]     - `blocking_queries` non-empty in `query_db` result → live blocking chain, act immediately.
[db]     - `waiting_queries == 0` AND `blocking_queries == []` → DB is **not** root cause, escalate to backend/network.
[db]     - Logs showing `Lock wait timeout exceeded` → transactions blocking each other.
[db]     
[db]     ## Safe Mitigations During Incident
[db]     
[db]     1. **Kill blocking transactions** — use `run_action(action="kill_blocking_queries")` **only if** `blocking_queries` is non-empty.
[db]     2. **Coordinate with Backend Agent** — identify if a recent deploy changed transaction scope or connection handling.
[db]     3. **Do NOT drop or truncate tables** — data integrity is paramount.
[db]     
[db]     ## Risk Assessment
[db]     
[db]     | Action | Risk Level | Reversible? |
[db]     |--------|-----------|------------|
[db]     | Kill blocking queries | Low | Yes |
[db]     | Rollback transaction | Low | Yes |
[db]     | Schema change | CRITICAL | No — defer to postmortem |
[db]     | Drop table / index | CRITICAL | No — forbidden during incident |
[db]     
[db]     ## Reporting Format
[db]     
[db]     - Lock wait count and deadlock count
[db]     - Blocking transaction IDs if available
[db]     - Actions taken
[db]     - Whether DB is confirmed as root cause
[db]     
[db]     [skill:query-performance]
[db]     ---
[db]     name: query-performance
[db]     description: >
[db]       Database query performance investigation for the DB specialist. Use this
[db]       when query_latency_p99 exceeds 500ms, slow query count is high, or
[db]       active connections approach the maximum. Covers slow query patterns,
[db]       emergency mitigations, and index recommendations.
[db]     metadata:
[db]       version: "1.0.0"
[db]       domain: sre
[db]       tags: [query, performance, database, db]
[db]     ---
[db]     
[db]     # Query Performance Investigation
[db]     
[db]     ## Investigation Steps
[db]     
[db]     1. Call `get_metrics(service="payment_db", metric="query_latency_p99", window="15m")`.
[db]     2. Call `get_metrics(service="payment_db", metric="active_connections", window="15m")`.
[db]     3. Call `get_metrics(service="payment_db", metric="slow_queries", window="15m")`.
[db]     
[db]     ## Interpreting Results
[db]     
[db]     - `query_latency_p99 > 500ms` → slow query problem, check indexes and execution plans.
[db]     - `active_connections > 80% of max_connections` → connection saturation.
[db]     - `slow_queries count > 10/min` → missing index or full table scan.
[db]     
[db]     ## Common Slow Query Patterns
[db]     
[db]     | Pattern | Symptom | Fix |
[db]     |---------|---------|-----|
[db]     | Missing index on `transactions` | Full table scan on writes | Add index (after incident) |
[db]     | Unparameterized queries | Plan cache misses | Code fix |
[db]     | N+1 query cascade | High query count, low individual latency | ORM fix |
[db]     | Batch inserts without lock | Lock escalation | Use row-level locking |
[db]     
[db]     ## Emergency Mitigations (during incident)
[db]     
[db]     - Kill long-running queries via `run_action(action="kill_slow_queries")`.
[db]     - Reduce connection pool size on application side to prevent pileup.
[db]     - Enable read replica routing for non-write queries if available.
[db]     
[db]     ## Reporting Format
[db]     
[db]     - Current P99 query latency
[db]     - Slow query count / type
[db]     - Whether kill action was taken
[db]     - Index recommendation for postmortem
[db]

[db]     [skill:uncertainty-protocol]
[db]     ---
[db]     name: uncertainty-protocol
[db]     description: >
[db]       Structured gap-check and confidence-scoring protocol for analyst agents.
[db]       Use this before writing any conclusion or hypothesis to ensure every claim
[db]       is backed by evidence and gaps are explicitly declared rather than filled
[db]       by speculation.
[db]     metadata:
[db]       version: "1.0.0"
[db]       domain: sre
[db]       tags: [uncertainty, protocol, shared]
[db]     ---
[db]     
[db]     # Uncertainty Protocol — Telemetry Analyst
[db]     
[db]     Before writing any conclusion or hypothesis, complete the following block exactly.
[db]     Do not skip it even if you believe the answer is obvious.
[db]     
[db]     ## Required Gap-Check Block
[db]     
[db]     After completing all tool calls for a question, produce:
[db]     
[db]     ```
[db]     EVIDENCE_ACCESSED:
[db]       - <tool_name>(<params>) → <key result in one line>
[db]       - ... (one line per call made this turn)
[db]     
[db]     GAPS:
[db]       - <question you cannot answer from the above results>
[db]       - ... (empty list = [] if nothing is missing)
[db]     
[db]     CONFIDENCE: <0.0–1.0>
[db]       Rule: must be ≤ 0.5 if GAPS is non-empty.
[db]       Rule: must cite at least one EVIDENCE_ACCESSED entry to justify values > 0.7.
[db]     ```
[db]     
[db]     ## When GAPS is non-empty
[db]     
[db]     Do **not** proceed to a conclusion. Instead write:
[db]     
[db]     ```
[db]     CLARIFICATION_NEEDED: <the single most important missing piece>
[db]     SUGGESTED_SOURCE: <which agent or tool could provide it>
[db]     ```
[db]     
[db]     Do not fabricate an answer to fill the gap. A stated gap is more useful
[db]     than a confident wrong conclusion.
[db]     
[db]     ## Telemetry-specific scope limits
[db]     
[db]     These questions are outside the telemetry agent's tool set. If asked about them,
[db]     list them in GAPS and suggest the appropriate agent:
[db]     
[db]     | Question | Correct agent |
[db]     |----------|---------------|
[db]     | Root cause of DB connection pool saturation | DB Specialist |
[db]     | Whether a deployment is responsible | Backend Engineer |
[db]     | Whether a rollback is safe | Backend Engineer + Verifier |
[db]     | Business impact in revenue terms | Comms Agent |
[db]     
[db]     ## Reporting Format
[db]     
[db]     Every conclusion must follow: **Observed → Evidence → Limitation**
[db]     
[db]     ```
[db]     OBSERVED:   error_rate on payment-service = 23.2% (from get_metrics)
[db]     EVIDENCE:   get_metrics("payment-service", metric="error_rate", window="15m") → 0.232
[db]     LIMITATION: cannot determine if deployment at 09:55 is causal without backend data
[db]     ```
[db]

[db]     [skill:lock-detection]
[db]     ---
[db]     name: lock-detection
[db]     description: >
[db]       Lock contention and deadlock analysis for database incidents. Use this
[db]       when observing lock_wait_timeout errors, sudden write queue buildup, or
[db]       P99 spikes on INSERT/UPDATE operations. Covers safe mitigations, risk
[db]       table, and blocking query kill procedure.
[db]     metadata:
[db]       version: "1.0.0"
[db]       domain: sre
[db]       tags: [locks, deadlocks, database, db]
[db]     ---
[db]     
[db]     # Lock Detection & Deadlock Analysis
[db]     
[db]     ## Symptoms
[db]     
[db]     - `lock_wait_timeout` errors in application logs.
[db]     - Sudden queue buildup on write operations.
[db]     - P99 spike on `INSERT`/`UPDATE` to `payments` or `transactions` table.
[db]     
[db]     ## Investigation Steps
[db]     
[db]     1. Call `get_metrics(service="{db_service}", metric="lock_wait_count", window="15m")`.
[db]     2. Call `get_metrics(service="{db_service}", metric="deadlock_count", window="15m")`.
[db]     3. Call `query_db(service="{db_service}", query_type="blocking_queries")` to get live pg_stat_activity data.
[db]     4. Call `query_db(service="{db_service}", query_type="pg_stat_activity")` for full connection picture.
[db]     5. Call `get_logs(service="{db_service}", level="ERROR", limit=10)` for lock timeout messages.
[db]     
[db]     ## Interpreting Results
[db]     
[db]     - `lock_wait_count > 50/min` → active lock contention.
[db]     - `deadlock_count > 0` → circular lock dependency, check transaction order in code.
[db]     - `blocking_queries` non-empty in `query_db` result → live blocking chain, act immediately.
[db]     - `waiting_queries == 0` AND `blocking_queries == []` → DB is **not** root cause, escalate to backend/network.
[db]     - Logs showing `Lock wait timeout exceeded` → transactions blocking each other.
[db]     
[db]     ## Safe Mitigations During Incident
[db]     
[db]     1. **Kill blocking transactions** — use `run_action(action="kill_blocking_queries")` **only if** `blocking_queries` is non-empty.
[db]     2. **Coordinate with Backend Agent** — identify if a recent deploy changed transaction scope or connection handling.
[db]     3. **Do NOT drop or truncate tables** — data integrity is paramount.
[db]     
[db]     ## Risk Assessment
[db]     
[db]     | Action | Risk Level | Reversible? |
[db]     |--------|-----------|------------|
[db]     | Kill blocking queries | Low | Yes |
[db]     | Rollback transaction | Low | Yes |
[db]     | Schema change | CRITICAL | No — defer to postmortem |
[db]     | Drop table / index | CRITICAL | No — forbidden during incident |
[db]     
[db]     ## Reporting Format
[db]     
[db]     - Lock wait count and deadlock count
[db]     - Blocking transaction IDs if available
[db]     - Actions taken
[db]     - Whether DB is confirmed as root cause
[db]

[db]       Database query performance investigation for the DB specialist. Use this
[db]       when query_latency_p99 exceeds 500ms, slow query count is high, or
[db]       active connections approach the maximum. Covers slow query patterns,
[db]       emergency mitigations, and index recommendations.
[db]     metadata:

[db]       domain: sre
[db]       tags: [query, performance, database, db]
[db]     ---
[db]     
[db]     # Query Performance Investigation
[db]     
[db]     ## Investigation Steps
[db]     
[db]     1. Call `get_metrics(service="payment_db", metric="query_latency_p99", window="15m")`.
[db]     2. Call `get_metrics(service="payment_db", metric="active_connections", window="15m")`.
[db]     3. Call `get_metrics(service="payment_db", metric="slow_queries", window="15m")`.
[db]     
[db]     ## Interpreting Results
[db]     
[db]     - `query_latency_p99 > 500ms` → slow query problem, check indexes and execution plans.
[db]     - `active_connections > 80% of max_connections` → connection saturation.
[db]     - `slow_queries count > 10/min` → missing index or full table scan.
[db]     
[db]     ## Common Slow Query Patterns
[db]     
[db]     | Pattern | Symptom | Fix |
[db]     |---------|---------|-----|
[db]     | Missing index on `transactions` | Full table scan on writes | Add index (after incident) |
[db]     | Unparameterized queries | Plan cache misses | Code fix |
[db]     | N+1 query cascade | High query count, low individual latency | ORM fix |
[db]     | Batch inserts without lock | Lock escalation | Use row-level locking |
[db]     
[db]     ## Emergency Mitigations (during incident)
[db]     
[db]     - Kill long-running queries via `run_action(action="kill_slow_queries")`.
[db]     - Reduce connection pool size on application side to prevent pileup.
[db]     - Enable read replica routing for non-write queries if available.
[db]     
[db]     ## Reporting Format
[db]     
[db]     - Current P99 query latency
[db]     - Slow query count / type
[db]     - Whether kill action was taken
[db]     - Index recommendation for postmortem
[db]

[db]     ---
[db]     name: data-access-protocol
[db]     description: >
[db]       Tool invocation discipline for all data-access tools (get_metrics, get_logs,
[db]       get_service_health, get_deployments, query_db). Use this to ensure every tool
[db]       call uses the exact canonical service name from the incident description.
[db]       Prevents tool errors and cross-agent correlation failures.
[db]     metadata:
[db]       version: "1.0.0"
[db]       domain: sre
[db]       tags: [data-access, protocol, shared]
[db]     ---
[db]     
[db]     # Data Access Protocol
[db]     
[db]     ## Tool Invocation Discipline
[db]     
[db]     When calling any data tool (`get_metrics`, `get_logs`, `get_service_health`,
[db]     `get_deployments`, `query_db`), you MUST pass the canonical service name as
[db]     the `service` argument.
[db]     
[db]     **Rule**: Use the **exact** service identifier from the incident description
[db]     verbatim (e.g. `"payment-service"`). Do not omit the `service` argument, do
[db]     not paraphrase the name, and do not substitute a generic placeholder.
[db]     
[db]     **Why this matters**: Omitting or misspelling the service name causes tools
[db]     to return an error — there is no default fallback. Agents will see
[db]     `"error": "required parameter 'service' is missing"` if the argument is
[db]     absent. Cross-agent correlation fails when different agents query different
[db]     service names for the same incident.
[db]     
[db]     ## Correct Pattern
[db]     
[db]     ```
[db]     get_metrics(service="payment-service")   # ✓ exact canonical name
[db]     get_logs(service="payment-service")      # ✓ same canonical name
[db]     get_deployments(service="payment-service")  # ✓ consistent
[db]     ```
[db]     
[db]     ## Incorrect Patterns
[db]     
[db]     ```
[db]     get_metrics()                   # ✗ missing service arg → tool returns error
[db]     get_metrics(service="payment")  # ✗ partial name → tool returns error
[db]     get_metrics(service="service")  # ✗ generic placeholder → tool returns error
[db]     ```
[db]     
[db]     ## Where to Find the Canonical Name
[db]     
[db]     The canonical service name appears in:
[db]     - The incident fixture: `spec.params.incident_fixture` → `services:` keys
[db]     - The SRE's initial incident description passed to you at delegation time
[db]     - The incident summary in your system context
[db]     
[db]     Use it verbatim. Do not normalise underscores to hyphens or vice versa unless
[db]     the fixture explicitly lists both as aliases.
[db]     
[db]     [skill:uncertainty-protocol]
[db]     ---
[db]     name: uncertainty-protocol
[db]     description: >
[db]       Structured gap-check and confidence-scoring protocol for analyst agents.
[db]       Use this before writing any conclusion or hypothesis to ensure every claim
[db]       is backed by evidence and gaps are explicitly declared rather than filled
[db]       by speculation.
[db]     metadata:
[db]       version: "1.0.0"
[db]       domain: sre
[db]       tags: [uncertainty, protocol, shared]
[db]     ---
[db]     
[db]     # Uncertainty Protocol — Telemetry Analyst
[db]     
[db]     Before writing any conclusion or hypothesis, complete the following block exactly.
[db]     Do not skip it even if you believe the answer is obvious.
[db]     
[db]     ## Required Gap-Check Block
[db]     
[db]     After completing all tool calls for a question, produce:
[db]     
[db]     ```
[db]     EVIDENCE_ACCESSED:
[db]       - <tool_name>(<params>) → <key result in one line>
[db]       - ... (one line per call made this turn)
[db]     
[db]     GAPS:
[db]       - <question you cannot answer from the above results>
[db]       - ... (empty list = [] if nothing is missing)
[db]     
[db]     CONFIDENCE: <0.0–1.0>
[db]       Rule: must be ≤ 0.5 if GAPS is non-empty.
[db]       Rule: must cite at least one EVIDENCE_ACCESSED entry to justify values > 0.7.
[db]     ```
[db]     
[db]     ## When GAPS is non-empty
[db]     
[db]     Do **not** proceed to a conclusion. Instead write:
[db]     
[db]     ```
[db]     CLARIFICATION_NEEDED: <the single most important missing piece>
[db]     SUGGESTED_SOURCE: <which agent or tool could provide it>
[db]     ```
[db]     
[db]     Do not fabricate an answer to fill the gap. A stated gap is more useful
[db]     than a confident wrong conclusion.
[db]     
[db]     ## Telemetry-specific scope limits
[db]     
[db]     These questions are outside the telemetry agent's tool set. If asked about them,
[db]     list them in GAPS and suggest the appropriate agent:
[db]     
[db]     | Question | Correct agent |
[db]     |----------|---------------|
[db]     | Root cause of DB connection pool saturation | DB Specialist |
[db]     | Whether a deployment is responsible | Backend Engineer |
[db]     | Whether a rollback is safe | Backend Engineer + Verifier |
[db]     | Business impact in revenue terms | Comms Agent |
[db]     
[db]     ## Reporting Format
[db]     
[db]     Every conclusion must follow: **Observed → Evidence → Limitation**
[db]     
[db]     ```
[db]     OBSERVED:   error_rate on payment-service = 23.2% (from get_metrics)
[db]     EVIDENCE:   get_metrics("payment-service", metric="error_rate", window="15m") → 0.232
[db]     LIMITATION: cannot determine if deployment at 09:55 is causal without backend data
[db]     ```
[db]     
[db]     [skill:memory-protocol]
[db]     ---
[db]     name: memory-protocol
[db]     description: >
[db]       Structured episodic memory protocol for agents operating in a multi-agent
[db]       system. Use this to write and read findings in a canonical format that
[db]       downstream agents can reliably retrieve. Prevents duplicate tool calls and
[db]       cross-agent correlation failures.
[db]     metadata:
[db]       version: "1.0.0"
[db]       domain: sre
[db]       tags: [memory, protocol, shared]
[db]     ---
[db]     
[db]     # Memory Protocol
[db]     
[db]     All agents share an episodic store. Unstructured writes cannot be reliably
[db]     retrieved downstream. Use this format for every write.
[db]     
[db]     ## Write format — Evidence Card
[db]     
[db]     Every time you write to memory, produce exactly one card per finding:
[db]     
[db]     ```
[db]     MEMORY_WRITE:
[db]       service:       <service name, e.g. payment-service>
[db]       metric:        <what was measured, e.g. p99_latency_ms>
[db]       value:         <observed value or range, e.g. 4200>
[db]       timestamp:     <ISO-8601 or "from run_id=<id>">
[db]       source_agent:  <your agent name>
[db]       tool_call:     <tool_name(params) that produced this value>
[db]       interpretation: <one-sentence meaning, e.g. "exceeds 2 000 ms SLO">
[db]     ```
[db]     
[db]     Write multiple cards if a single tool call yields multiple distinct facts.
[db]     Do not combine unrelated facts in one card.
[db]     
[db]     ## Read format — Structured Query
[db]     
[db]     Before calling a tool that another agent may already have run, query memory:
[db]     
[db]     ```
[db]     MEMORY_READ:
[db]       service: <service name>
[db]       metric:  <metric name>
[db]     ```
[db]     
[db]     If the store returns a match, use it and note:
[db]     
[db]     ```
[db]     RECALLED: <service>/<metric> = <value> (from <source_agent>)
[db]     ```
[db]     
[db]     Do not re-run the same tool call if a valid recall exists.
[db]     
[db]     ## What not to write
[db]     
[db]     - Do not write summaries or prose paragraphs to memory.
[db]     - Do not write hypotheses or confidence scores.
[db]     - Do not write tool errors (write `GAPS` in the uncertainty block instead).

[db]     - Escalation routing decisions (which specialist was engaged and why)

[db]     # Query Performance Investigation
[db]     
[db]     ## Investigation Steps
[db]     
[db]     1. Call `get_metrics(service="payment_db", metric="query_latency_p99", window="15m")`.
[db]     2. Call `get_metrics(service="payment_db", metric="active_connections", window="15m")`.
[db]     3. Call `get_metrics(service="payment_db", metric="slow_queries", window="15m")`.
[db]     
[db]     ## Interpreting Results
[db]     
[db]     - `query_latency_p99 > 500ms` → slow query problem, check indexes and execution plans.
[db]     - `active_connections > 80% of max_connections` → connection saturation.
[db]     - `slow_queries count > 10/min` → missing index or full table scan.

[db]     ## Common Slow Query Patterns
[db]     
[db]     | Pattern | Symptom | Fix |
[db]     |---------|---------|-----|
[db]     | Missing index on `transactions` | Full table scan on writes | Add index (after incident) |
[db]     | Unparameterized queries | Plan cache misses | Code fix |
[db]     | N+1 query cascade | High query count, low individual latency | ORM fix |
[db]     | Batch inserts without lock | Lock escalation | Use row-level locking |
[db]     
[db]     ## Emergency Mitigations (during incident)
[db]     
[db]     - Kill long-running queries via `run_action(action="kill_slow_queries")`.
[db]     - Reduce connection pool size on application side to prevent pileup.
[db]     - Enable read replica routing for non-write queries if available.

[db]     ## Reporting Format
[db]

[db]     - Slow query count / type

[db]       Tool invocation discipline for all data-access tools (get_metrics, get_logs,
[db]       get_service_health, get_deployments, query_db). Use this to ensure every tool

[db]     metadata:

[db]     ---
[db]     
[db]     # Data Access Protocol
[db]     
[db]     ## Tool Invocation Discipline
[db]     
[db]     When calling any data tool (`get_metrics`, `get_logs`, `get_service_health`,
[db]     `get_deployments`, `query_db`), you MUST pass the canonical service name as
[db]     the `service` argument.
[db]     
[db]     **Rule**: Use the **exact** service identifier from the incident description
[db]     verbatim (e.g. `"payment-service"`). Do not omit the `service` argument, do
[db]     not paraphrase the name, and do not substitute a generic placeholder.
[db]     
[db]     **Why this matters**: Omitting or misspelling the service name causes tools
[db]     to return an error — there is no default fallback. Agents will see
[db]     `"error": "required parameter 'service' is missing"` if the argument is
[db]     absent. Cross-agent correlation fails when different agents query different
[db]     service names for the same incident.
[db]     
[db]     ## Correct Pattern
[db]     
[db]     ```
[db]     get_metrics(service="payment-service")   # ✓ exact canonical name
[db]     get_logs(service="payment-service")      # ✓ same canonical name
[db]     get_deployments(service="payment-service")  # ✓ consistent
[db]     ```
[db]     
[db]     ## Incorrect Patterns
[db]     
[db]     ```
[db]     get_metrics()                   # ✗ missing service arg → tool returns error
[db]     get_metrics(service="payment")  # ✗ partial name → tool returns error
[db]     get_metrics(service="service")  # ✗ generic placeholder → tool returns error
[db]     ```
[db]     
[db]     ## Where to Find the Canonical Name
[db]     
[db]     The canonical service name appears in:
[db]     - The incident fixture: `spec.params.incident_fixture` → `services:` keys
[db]     - The SRE's initial incident description passed to you at delegation time
[db]     - The incident summary in your system context
[db]     
[db]     Use it verbatim. Do not normalise underscores to hyphens or vice versa unless
[db]     the fixture explicitly lists both as aliases.
[db]     
[db]     [skill:uncertainty-protocol]
[db]     ---
[db]     name: uncertainty-protocol
[db]     description: >
[db]       Structured gap-check and confidence-scoring protocol for analyst agents.
[db]       Use this before writing any conclusion or hypothesis to ensure every claim
[db]       is backed by evidence and gaps are explicitly declared rather than filled
[db]       by speculation.
[db]     metadata:
[db]       version: "1.0.0"
[db]       domain: sre
[db]       tags: [uncertainty, protocol, shared]
[db]     ---
[db]     
[db]     # Uncertainty Protocol — Telemetry Analyst
[db]     
[db]     Before writing any conclusion or hypothesis, complete the following block exactly.
[db]     Do not skip it even if you believe the answer is obvious.
[db]     
[db]     ## Required Gap-Check Block
[db]     
[db]     After completing all tool calls for a question, produce:
[db]     
[db]     ```
[db]     EVIDENCE_ACCESSED:
[db]       - <tool_name>(<params>) → <key result in one line>
[db]       - ... (one line per call made this turn)
[db]     
[db]     GAPS:
[db]       - <question you cannot answer from the above results>
[db]       - ... (empty list = [] if nothing is missing)
[db]     
[db]     CONFIDENCE: <0.0–1.0>
[db]       Rule: must be ≤ 0.5 if GAPS is non-empty.
[db]       Rule: must cite at least one EVIDENCE_ACCESSED entry to justify values > 0.7.
[db]     ```
[db]     
[db]     ## When GAPS is non-empty
[db]     
[db]     Do **not** proceed to a conclusion. Instead write:
[db]     
[db]     ```
[db]     CLARIFICATION_NEEDED: <the single most important missing piece>
[db]     SUGGESTED_SOURCE: <which agent or tool could provide it>
[db]     ```
[db]     
[db]     Do not fabricate an answer to fill the gap. A stated gap is more useful
[db]     than a confident wrong conclusion.
[db]     
[db]     ## Telemetry-specific scope limits
[db]     
[db]     These questions are outside the telemetry agent's tool set. If asked about them,
[db]     list them in GAPS and suggest the appropriate agent:
[db]     
[db]     | Question | Correct agent |
[db]     |----------|---------------|
[db]     | Root cause of DB connection pool saturation | DB Specialist |
[db]     | Whether a deployment is responsible | Backend Engineer |
[db]     | Whether a rollback is safe | Backend Engineer + Verifier |
[db]     | Business impact in revenue terms | Comms Agent |
[db]     
[db]     ## Reporting Format
[db]     
[db]     Every conclusion must follow: **Observed → Evidence → Limitation**
[db]     
[db]     ```
[db]     OBSERVED:   error_rate on payment-service = 23.2% (from get_metrics)
[db]     EVIDENCE:   get_metrics("payment-service", metric="error_rate", window="15m") → 0.232
[db]     LIMITATION: cannot determine if deployment at 09:55 is causal without backend data
[db]     ```
[db]

[db]     # Memory Protocol
[db]     
[db]     All agents share an episodic store. Unstructured writes cannot be reliably
[db]     retrieved downstream. Use this format for every write.
[db]     
[db]     ## Write format — Evidence Card
[db]     
[db]     Every time you write to memory, produce exactly one card per finding:
[db]     
[db]     ```
[db]     MEMORY_WRITE:
[db]       service:       <service name, e.g. payment-service>
[db]       metric:        <what was measured, e.g. p99_latency_ms>
[db]       value:         <observed value or range, e.g. 4200>
[db]       timestamp:     <ISO-8601 or "from run_id=<id>">
[db]       source_agent:  <your agent name>
[db]       tool_call:     <tool_name(params) that produced this value>
[db]       interpretation: <one-sentence meaning, e.g. "exceeds 2 000 ms SLO">
[db]     ```
[db]     
[db]     Write multiple cards if a single tool call yields multiple distinct facts.
[db]     Do not combine unrelated facts in one card.
[db]     
[db]     ## Read format — Structured Query
[db]     
[db]     Before calling a tool that another agent may already have run, query memory:
[db]     
[db]     ```
[db]     MEMORY_READ:
[db]       service: <service name>
[db]       metric:  <metric name>
[db]     ```
[db]     
[db]     If the store returns a match, use it and note:
[db]     
[db]     ```
[db]     RECALLED: <service>/<metric> = <value> (from <source_agent>)
[db]     ```
[db]     
[db]     Do not re-run the same tool call if a valid recall exists.
[db]     
[db]     ## What not to write
[db]     
[db]     - Do not write summaries or prose paragraphs to memory.
[db]     - Do not write hypotheses or confidence scores.
[db]     - Do not write tool errors (write `GAPS` in the uncertainty block instead).

[db]     ---
[db]     name: lock-detection
[db]     description: >
[db]       Lock contention and deadlock analysis for database incidents. Use this
[db]       when observing lock_wait_timeout errors, sudden write queue buildup, or
[db]       P99 spikes on INSERT/UPDATE operations. Covers safe mitigations, risk
[db]       table, and blocking query kill procedure.
[db]     metadata:
[db]       version: "1.0.0"
[db]       domain: sre
[db]       tags: [locks, deadlocks, database, db]
[db]     ---
[db]     
[db]     # Lock Detection & Deadlock Analysis
[db]     
[db]     ## Symptoms
[db]     
[db]     - `lock_wait_timeout` errors in application logs.
[db]     - Sudden queue buildup on write operations.
[db]     - P99 spike on `INSERT`/`UPDATE` to `payments` or `transactions` table.
[db]     
[db]     ## Investigation Steps
[db]     
[db]     1. Call `get_metrics(service="{db_service}", metric="lock_wait_count", window="15m")`.
[db]     2. Call `get_metrics(service="{db_service}", metric="deadlock_count", window="15m")`.
[db]     3. Call `query_db(service="{db_service}", query_type="blocking_queries")` to get live pg_stat_activity data.
[db]     4. Call `query_db(service="{db_service}", query_type="pg_stat_activity")` for full connection picture.
[db]     5. Call `get_logs(service="{db_service}", level="ERROR", limit=10)` for lock timeout messages.
[db]     
[db]     ## Interpreting Results
[db]     
[db]     - `lock_wait_count > 50/min` → active lock contention.
[db]     - `deadlock_count > 0` → circular lock dependency, check transaction order in code.
[db]     - `blocking_queries` non-empty in `query_db` result → live blocking chain, act immediately.
[db]     - `waiting_queries == 0` AND `blocking_queries == []` → DB is **not** root cause, escalate to backend/network.
[db]     - Logs showing `Lock wait timeout exceeded` → transactions blocking each other.
[db]     
[db]     ## Safe Mitigations During Incident
[db]     
[db]     1. **Kill blocking transactions** — use `run_action(action="kill_blocking_queries")` **only if** `blocking_queries` is non-empty.
[db]     2. **Coordinate with Backend Agent** — identify if a recent deploy changed transaction scope or connection handling.
[db]     3. **Do NOT drop or truncate tables** — data integrity is paramount.
[db]     
[db]     ## Risk Assessment
[db]     
[db]     | Action | Risk Level | Reversible? |
[db]     |--------|-----------|------------|
[db]     | Kill blocking queries | Low | Yes |
[db]     | Rollback transaction | Low | Yes |
[db]     | Schema change | CRITICAL | No — defer to postmortem |
[db]     | Drop table / index | CRITICAL | No — forbidden during incident |
[db]     
[db]     ## Reporting Format
[db]     
[db]     - Lock wait count and deadlock count
[db]     - Blocking transaction IDs if available
[db]     - Actions taken
[db]     - Whether DB is confirmed as root cause
[db]

[db]     CONFIDENCE: <0.0–1.0>
[db]       Rule: must be ≤ 0.5 if GAPS is non-empty.

[db]     SUGGESTED_SOURCE: <which agent or tool could provide it>

[db]     than a confident wrong conclusion.

[sre]     [skill:triage-protocol]
[sre]     ---
[sre]     name: triage-protocol
[sre]     description: >
[sre]       Step-by-step incident triage protocol for the SRE orchestrator. Use this
[sre]       to guide parallel investigation dispatch, root-cause synthesis, mandatory
[sre]       verification gate, and final report. Applies to any SEV1/SEV2/SEV3 incident.
[sre]     metadata:
[sre]       version: "1.0.0"
[sre]       domain: sre
[sre]       tags: [triage, protocol, orchestrator]
[sre]     ---
[sre]     
[sre]     # Incident Triage Protocol
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 1 — Initial Assessment (< 2 minutes)
[sre]     - Confirm incident symptoms (latency, error rates, conversion impact).
[sre]     - Check if this is a new event or regression from a known issue.
[sre]     - Set initial severity (SEV1 / SEV2 / SEV3) based on customer impact.
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 2 — Parallel Investigation Delegation
[sre]     Immediately dispatch tasks to specialist agents:
[sre]     - **Telemetry Agent**: analyse span/trace latency breakdown, error rates, anomaly correlation.
[sre]     - **Backend Agent**: check recent deployments, connection pool usage, config changes.
[sre]     - **DB Agent**: inspect slow queries, lock contention, connection pool saturation.
[sre]     - **Comms Agent**: draft initial status-page update and internal War Room message.
[sre]     
[sre]     Do NOT wait for one agent to finish before calling the next. Dispatch all in sequence.
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 3 — Collect Findings
[sre]     Wait for each specialist to return a result, then aggregate.
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 4 — Root Cause & Action Plan
[sre]     Based on collected evidence, identify the most likely root cause and write:
[sre]     - Confirmed or suspected root cause
[sre]     - Immediate mitigation (rollback / feature flag / query kill)
[sre]     - Follow-up actions (monitoring, postmortem)
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 5 — Verification Gate (MANDATORY before any remediation action)
[sre]     Before calling `run_action`, you MUST delegate to the Verifier agent:
[sre]     - Call `delegate_to_verifier` with your root cause summary and action plan.
[sre]     - Wait for the Verifier response. It will contain one of:
[sre]       - `VERIFICATION: APPROVED` — proceed to Step 6
[sre]       - `VERIFICATION: FLAGGED — <reason>` — address the flagged concern, then re-verify
[sre]       - `VERIFICATION: REJECTED — <reason>` — do NOT proceed; escalate to incident commander
[sre]     - **NEVER call `run_action` without a prior `VERIFICATION: APPROVED` in the current session.**
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 6 — Final Report
[sre]     Produce a single consolidated triage report for the incident commander.
[sre]     Include the verification outcome (e.g. "Verified by Verifier — APPROVED").
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 7 — Remediation Action
[sre]     Only after receiving `VERIFICATION: APPROVED`, call `run_action` with the approved plan.
[sre]

[sre]     [skill:data-access-protocol]
[sre]     ---
[sre]     name: data-access-protocol
[sre]     description: >
[sre]       Tool invocation discipline for all data-access tools (get_metrics, get_logs,
[sre]       get_service_health, get_deployments, query_db). Use this to ensure every tool
[sre]       call uses the exact canonical service name from the incident description.
[sre]       Prevents tool errors and cross-agent correlation failures.
[sre]     metadata:
[sre]       version: "1.0.0"
[sre]       domain: sre
[sre]       tags: [data-access, protocol, shared]
[sre]     ---
[sre]     
[sre]     # Data Access Protocol
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Tool Invocation Discipline
[sre]     
[sre]     When calling any data tool (`get_metrics`, `get_logs`, `get_service_health`,
[sre]     `get_deployments`, `query_db`), you MUST pass the canonical service name as
[sre]     the `service` argument.
[sre]     
[sre]     **Rule**: Use the **exact** service identifier from the incident description
[sre]     verbatim (e.g. `"payment-service"`). Do not omit the `service` argument, do
[sre]     not paraphrase the name, and do not substitute a generic placeholder.
[sre]     
[sre]     **Why this matters**: Omitting or misspelling the service name causes tools
[sre]     to return an error — there is no default fallback. Agents will see
[sre]     `"error": "required parameter 'service' is missing"` if the argument is
[sre]     absent. Cross-agent correlation fails when different agents query different
[sre]     service names for the same incident.
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Correct Pattern
[sre]     
[sre]     ```
[sre]     get_metrics(service="payment-service")   # ✓ exact canonical name
[sre]     get_logs(service="payment-service")      # ✓ same canonical name
[sre]     get_deployments(service="payment-service")  # ✓ consistent
[sre]     ```
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Incorrect Patterns
[sre]     
[sre]     ```
[sre]     get_metrics()                   # ✗ missing service arg → tool returns error
[sre]     get_metrics(service="payment")  # ✗ partial name → tool returns error
[sre]     get_metrics(service="service")  # ✗ generic placeholder → tool returns error
[sre]     ```
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Where to Find the Canonical Name
[sre]     
[sre]     The canonical service name appears in:
[sre]     - The incident fixture: `spec.params.incident_fixture` → `services:` keys
[sre]     - The SRE's initial incident description passed to you at delegation time
[sre]     - The incident summary in your system context
[sre]     
[sre]     Use it verbatim. Do not normalise underscores to hyphens or vice versa unless
[sre]     the fixture explicitly lists both as aliases.
[sre]   [user]

[comms]     ---
[comms]     name: memory-protocol
[comms]     description: >
[comms]       Structured episodic memory protocol for agents operating in a multi-agent
[comms]       system. Use this to write and read findings in a canonical format that
[comms]       downstream agents can reliably retrieve. Prevents duplicate tool calls and
[comms]       cross-agent correlation failures.
[comms]     metadata:
[comms]       version: "1.0.0"
[comms]       domain: sre
[comms]       tags: [memory, protocol, shared]
[comms]     ---
[comms]     
[comms]     # Memory Protocol
[comms]     
[comms]     All agents share an episodic store. Unstructured writes cannot be reliably
[comms]     retrieved downstream. Use this format for every write.
[comms]     
[comms]     ## Write format — Evidence Card
[comms]     
[comms]     Every time you write to memory, produce exactly one card per finding:
[comms]     
[comms]     ```
[comms]     MEMORY_WRITE:
[comms]       service:       <service name, e.g. payment-service>
[comms]       metric:        <what was measured, e.g. p99_latency_ms>
[comms]       value:         <observed value or range, e.g. 4200>
[comms]       timestamp:     <ISO-8601 or "from run_id=<id>">
[comms]       source_agent:  <your agent name>
[comms]       tool_call:     <tool_name(params) that produced this value>
[comms]       interpretation: <one-sentence meaning, e.g. "exceeds 2 000 ms SLO">
[comms]     ```
[comms]     
[comms]     Write multiple cards if a single tool call yields multiple distinct facts.
[comms]     Do not combine unrelated facts in one card.
[comms]     
[comms]     ## Read format — Structured Query
[comms]     
[comms]     Before calling a tool that another agent may already have run, query memory:
[comms]     
[comms]     ```
[comms]     MEMORY_READ:
[comms]       service: <service name>
[comms]       metric:  <metric name>
[comms]     ```
[comms]     
[comms]     If the store returns a match, use it and note:
[comms]     
[comms]     ```
[comms]     RECALLED: <service>/<metric> = <value> (from <source_agent>)
[comms]     ```
[comms]     
[comms]     Do not re-run the same tool call if a valid recall exists.
[comms]     
[comms]     ## What not to write
[comms]     
[comms]     - Do not write summaries or prose paragraphs to memory.
[comms]     - Do not write hypotheses or confidence scores.
[comms]     - Do not write tool errors (write `GAPS` in the uncertainty block instead).
[comms]     
[comms]     ## SRE-specific guidance
[comms]     
[comms]     The SRE agent's writes should cover:
[comms]     - Severity classification decisions and the evidence that triggered them
[comms]     - Escalation routing decisions (which specialist was engaged and why)
[comms]     - Time-to-first-response milestones

[comms]     ---
[comms]     
[comms]     # Data Access Protocol
[comms]     
[comms]     ## Tool Invocation Discipline
[comms]     
[comms]     When calling any data tool (`get_metrics`, `get_logs`, `get_service_health`,
[comms]     `get_deployments`, `query_db`), you MUST pass the canonical service name as
[comms]     the `service` argument.
[comms]     
[comms]     **Rule**: Use the **exact** service identifier from the incident description
[comms]     verbatim (e.g. `"payment-service"`). Do not omit the `service` argument, do
[comms]     not paraphrase the name, and do not substitute a generic placeholder.
[comms]     
[comms]     **Why this matters**: Omitting or misspelling the service name causes tools
[comms]     to return an error — there is no default fallback. Agents will see
[comms]     `"error": "required parameter 'service' is missing"` if the argument is
[comms]     absent. Cross-agent correlation fails when different agents query different
[comms]     service names for the same incident.
[comms]     
[comms]     ## Correct Pattern
[comms]     
[comms]     ```
[comms]     get_metrics(service="payment-service")   # ✓ exact canonical name
[comms]     get_logs(service="payment-service")      # ✓ same canonical name
[comms]     get_deployments(service="payment-service")  # ✓ consistent
[comms]     ```
[comms]     
[comms]     ## Incorrect Patterns
[comms]     
[comms]     ```
[comms]     get_metrics()                   # ✗ missing service arg → tool returns error
[comms]     get_metrics(service="payment")  # ✗ partial name → tool returns error
[comms]     get_metrics(service="service")  # ✗ generic placeholder → tool returns error
[comms]     ```
[comms]     
[comms]     ## Where to Find the Canonical Name
[comms]     
[comms]     The canonical service name appears in:
[comms]     - The incident fixture: `spec.params.incident_fixture` → `services:` keys
[comms]     - The SRE's initial incident description passed to you at delegation time
[comms]     - The incident summary in your system context
[comms]     
[comms]     Use it verbatim. Do not normalise underscores to hyphens or vice versa unless
[comms]     the fixture explicitly lists both as aliases.

[sre]     [skill:triage-protocol]
[sre]     ---
[sre]     name: triage-protocol
[sre]     description: >
[sre]       Step-by-step incident triage protocol for the SRE orchestrator. Use this
[sre]       to guide parallel investigation dispatch, root-cause synthesis, mandatory
[sre]       verification gate, and final report. Applies to any SEV1/SEV2/SEV3 incident.
[sre]     metadata:
[sre]       version: "1.0.0"
[sre]       domain: sre
[sre]       tags: [triage, protocol, orchestrator]
[sre]     ---
[sre]     
[sre]     # Incident Triage Protocol
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 1 — Initial Assessment (< 2 minutes)
[sre]     - Confirm incident symptoms (latency, error rates, conversion impact).
[sre]     - Check if this is a new event or regression from a known issue.
[sre]     - Set initial severity (SEV1 / SEV2 / SEV3) based on customer impact.
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 2 — Parallel Investigation Delegation
[sre]     Immediately dispatch tasks to specialist agents:
[sre]     - **Telemetry Agent**: analyse span/trace latency breakdown, error rates, anomaly correlation.
[sre]     - **Backend Agent**: check recent deployments, connection pool usage, config changes.
[sre]     - **DB Agent**: inspect slow queries, lock contention, connection pool saturation.
[sre]     - **Comms Agent**: draft initial status-page update and internal War Room message.
[sre]     
[sre]     Do NOT wait for one agent to finish before calling the next. Dispatch all in sequence.
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 3 — Collect Findings
[sre]     Wait for each specialist to return a result, then aggregate.
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 4 — Root Cause & Action Plan
[sre]     Based on collected evidence, identify the most likely root cause and write:
[sre]     - Confirmed or suspected root cause
[sre]     - Immediate mitigation (rollback / feature flag / query kill)
[sre]     - Follow-up actions (monitoring, postmortem)
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 5 — Verification Gate (MANDATORY before any remediation action)
[sre]     Before calling `run_action`, you MUST delegate to the Verifier agent:
[sre]     - Call `delegate_to_verifier` with your root cause summary and action plan.
[sre]     - Wait for the Verifier response. It will contain one of:
[sre]       - `VERIFICATION: APPROVED` — proceed to Step 6
[sre]       - `VERIFICATION: FLAGGED — <reason>` — address the flagged concern, then re-verify
[sre]       - `VERIFICATION: REJECTED — <reason>` — do NOT proceed; escalate to incident commander
[sre]     - **NEVER call `run_action` without a prior `VERIFICATION: APPROVED` in the current session.**
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 6 — Final Report
[sre]     Produce a single consolidated triage report for the incident commander.
[sre]     Include the verification outcome (e.g. "Verified by Verifier — APPROVED").
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 7 — Remediation Action
[sre]     Only after receiving `VERIFICATION: APPROVED`, call `run_action` with the approved plan.
[sre]

[sre]     # Data Access Protocol
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Tool Invocation Discipline
[sre]     
[sre]     When calling any data tool (`get_metrics`, `get_logs`, `get_service_health`,
[sre]     `get_deployments`, `query_db`), you MUST pass the canonical service name as
[sre]     the `service` argument.
[sre]     
[sre]     **Rule**: Use the **exact** service identifier from the incident description
[sre]     verbatim (e.g. `"payment-service"`). Do not omit the `service` argument, do
[sre]     not paraphrase the name, and do not substitute a generic placeholder.
[sre]     
[sre]     **Why this matters**: Omitting or misspelling the service name causes tools
[sre]     to return an error — there is no default fallback. Agents will see
[sre]     `"error": "required parameter 'service' is missing"` if the argument is
[sre]     absent. Cross-agent correlation fails when different agents query different
[sre]     service names for the same incident.
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Correct Pattern
[sre]     
[sre]     ```
[sre]     get_metrics(service="payment-service")   # ✓ exact canonical name
[sre]     get_logs(service="payment-service")      # ✓ same canonical name
[sre]     get_deployments(service="payment-service")  # ✓ consistent
[sre]     ```
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Incorrect Patterns
[sre]     
[sre]     ```
[sre]     get_metrics()                   # ✗ missing service arg → tool returns error
[sre]     get_metrics(service="payment")  # ✗ partial name → tool returns error
[sre]     get_metrics(service="service")  # ✗ generic placeholder → tool returns error

[verifier]     
[verifier]     # Risk Assessment for Incident Actions
[verifier]     
[verifier]     ## Risk Classification
[verifier]     
[verifier]     | Risk Level | Definition | Approval Required |
[verifier]     |-----------|-----------|------------------|
[verifier]     | LOW | Reversible, no data impact, isolated to one service | On-call SRE |
[verifier]     | MEDIUM | May impact multiple services, reversible with effort | SRE Lead |
[verifier]     | HIGH | Potential data loss, extended downtime, irreversible | VP Engineering |
[verifier]     | CRITICAL | Data corruption, security breach, compliance violation | CEO + Legal |
[verifier]     
[verifier]     ## Action Risk Table
[verifier]     
[verifier]     | Action | Risk Level | Notes |
[verifier]     |--------|-----------|-------|
[verifier]     | Kill slow query | LOW | Reversible, may retry |
[verifier]     | Feature flag disable | LOW | Instant rollback available |
[verifier]     | Service rollback | LOW | Provided tests pass |
[verifier]     | Scale out pods | LOW | Cost impact only |
[verifier]     | Kill all connections | MEDIUM | Brief service blip |
[verifier]     | Disable payment method | MEDIUM | Revenue impact, user-visible |
[verifier]     | Restart payment service | MEDIUM | Brief downtime |
[verifier]     | Schema migration | HIGH | Irreversible, needs downtime |
[verifier]     | Drop table or index | CRITICAL | Data loss, FORBIDDEN during incident |
[verifier]     
[verifier]     ## Evidence Standards
[verifier]     
[verifier]     For a recommendation to be actionable, it must be supported by:
[verifier]     - At least one quantitative metric (not just log messages)
[verifier]     - Clear temporal correlation (issue started after event X)
[verifier]     - No contradicting evidence from other agents
[verifier]     
[verifier]     ## Checklist Before Approving High-Risk Actions
[verifier]     
[verifier]     - [ ] Root cause confirmed by ≥ 2 independent signals
[verifier]     - [ ] Rollback plan documented
[verifier]     - [ ] Customer impact of action estimated
[verifier]     - [ ] SRE Lead notified
[verifier]

[verifier]     ---
[verifier]     name: verification-checklist
[verifier]     description: >
[verifier]       Pre-approval checklist and logical consistency rules for the verifier agent.
[verifier]       Use this before approving a triage report: verify evidence completeness,
[verifier]       check that mitigation matches root cause, and identify escalation triggers.
[verifier]       Returns APPROVED, FLAGGED, or BLOCKED.
[verifier]     metadata:

[verifier]       tags: [verification, checklist, verifier, approval]
[verifier]     ---
[verifier]     
[verifier]     # Triage Verification Checklist
[verifier]     
[verifier]     ## Evidence Completeness
[verifier]     
[verifier]     Before approving a final triage report, verify:
[verifier]     
[verifier]     - [ ] Telemetry agent confirmed which service/span is slow (internal vs external)
[verifier]     - [ ] Backend agent confirmed or ruled out a recent deployment as root cause
[verifier]     - [ ] DB agent confirmed or ruled out database contention
[verifier]     - [ ] At least one concrete metric value justifies the root cause conclusion
[verifier]     - [ ] Proposed mitigation is proportional to the confirmed root cause
[verifier]     
[verifier]     ## Logical Consistency Rules
[verifier]     
[verifier]     1. **Root cause must match evidence**: If the conclusion is "DB contention" but DB latency metrics show normal values, flag as inconsistent.
[verifier]     2. **Mitigation must target root cause**: If root cause is "external gateway timeout", rolling back a recent deploy is not the right fix — flag it.
[verifier]     3. **Risk must be acknowledged**: Any mitigation that could cause data loss or extended downtime must be explicitly flagged.
[verifier]     
[verifier]     ## Escalation Triggers
[verifier]     
[verifier]     Flag these issues immediately to the SRE Lead:
[verifier]     - Proposed action involves schema change or data deletion.
[verifier]     - Evidence is contradictory between agents.
[verifier]     - Incident has been active > 30 min with no confirmed root cause.
[verifier]     - Any agent suggests a mitigation not in the approved playbook.
[verifier]     
[verifier]     ## Verification Output Format
[verifier]     
[verifier]     Report back:
[verifier]     - **APPROVED** — evidence supports conclusion, mitigation is safe.
[verifier]     - **FLAGGED** — specific inconsistency or risk identified (describe it).
[verifier]     - **BLOCKED** — critical safety concern, do not proceed (describe it).

[sre]     ---
[sre]     name: triage-protocol
[sre]     description: >
[sre]       Step-by-step incident triage protocol for the SRE orchestrator. Use this
[sre]       to guide parallel investigation dispatch, root-cause synthesis, mandatory
[sre]       verification gate, and final report. Applies to any SEV1/SEV2/SEV3 incident.
[sre]     metadata:
[sre]       version: "1.0.0"
[sre]       domain: sre
[sre]       tags: [triage, protocol, orchestrator]
[sre]     ---
[sre]     
[sre]     # Incident Triage Protocol
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 1 — Initial Assessment (< 2 minutes)
[sre]     - Confirm incident symptoms (latency, error rates, conversion impact).
[sre]     - Check if this is a new event or regression from a known issue.
[sre]     - Set initial severity (SEV1 / SEV2 / SEV3) based on customer impact.
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 2 — Parallel Investigation Delegation
[sre]     Immediately dispatch tasks to specialist agents:
[sre]     - **Telemetry Agent**: analyse span/trace latency breakdown, error rates, anomaly correlation.
[sre]     - **Backend Agent**: check recent deployments, connection pool usage, config changes.
[sre]     - **DB Agent**: inspect slow queries, lock contention, connection pool saturation.
[sre]     - **Comms Agent**: draft initial status-page update and internal War Room message.
[sre]     
[sre]     Do NOT wait for one agent to finish before calling the next. Dispatch all in sequence.
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 3 — Collect Findings
[sre]     Wait for each specialist to return a result, then aggregate.
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 4 — Root Cause & Action Plan
[sre]     Based on collected evidence, identify the most likely root cause and write:
[sre]     - Confirmed or suspected root cause
[sre]     - Immediate mitigation (rollback / feature flag / query kill)
[sre]     - Follow-up actions (monitoring, postmortem)
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 5 — Verification Gate (MANDATORY before any remediation action)
[sre]     Before calling `run_action`, you MUST delegate to the Verifier agent:
[sre]     - Call `delegate_to_verifier` with your root cause summary and action plan.
[sre]     - Wait for the Verifier response. It will contain one of:
[sre]       - `VERIFICATION: APPROVED` — proceed to Step 6
[sre]       - `VERIFICATION: FLAGGED — <reason>` — address the flagged concern, then re-verify
[sre]       - `VERIFICATION: REJECTED — <reason>` — do NOT proceed; escalate to incident commander
[sre]     - **NEVER call `run_action` without a prior `VERIFICATION: APPROVED` in the current session.**
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 6 — Final Report
[sre]     Produce a single consolidated triage report for the incident commander.
[sre]     Include the verification outcome (e.g. "Verified by Verifier — APPROVED").
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Step 7 — Remediation Action
[sre]     Only after receiving `VERIFICATION: APPROVED`, call `run_action` with the approved plan.
[sre]

[sre]     ---
[sre]     name: memory-protocol
[sre]     description: >
[sre]       Structured episodic memory protocol for agents operating in a multi-agent
[sre]       system. Use this to write and read findings in a canonical format that
[sre]       downstream agents can reliably retrieve. Prevents duplicate tool calls and
[sre]       cross-agent correlation failures.
[sre]     metadata:
[sre]       version: "1.0.0"
[sre]       domain: sre
[sre]       tags: [memory, protocol, shared]
[sre]     ---
[sre]     
[sre]     # Memory Protocol
[sre]     
[sre]     All agents share an episodic store. Unstructured writes cannot be reliably
[sre]     retrieved downstream. Use this format for every write.
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Write format — Evidence Card
[sre]     
[sre]     Every time you write to memory, produce exactly one card per finding:
[sre]     
[sre]     ```
[sre]     MEMORY_WRITE:
[sre]       service:       <service name, e.g. payment-service>
[sre]       metric:        <what was measured, e.g. p99_latency_ms>
[sre]       value:         <observed value or range, e.g. 4200>
[sre]       timestamp:     <ISO-8601 or "from run_id=<id>">
[sre]       source_agent:  <your agent name>
[sre]       tool_call:     <tool_name(params) that produced this value>
[sre]       interpretation: <one-sentence meaning, e.g. "exceeds 2 000 ms SLO">
[sre]     ```
[sre]     
[sre]     Write multiple cards if a single tool call yields multiple distinct facts.
[sre]     Do not combine unrelated facts in one card.
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Read format — Structured Query
[sre]     
[sre]     Before calling a tool that another agent may already have run, query memory:
[sre]     
[sre]     ```
[sre]     MEMORY_READ:
[sre]       service: <service name>
[sre]       metric:  <metric name>
[sre]     ```
[sre]     
[sre]     If the store returns a match, use it and note:
[sre]     
[sre]     ```
[sre]     RECALLED: <service>/<metric> = <value> (from <source_agent>)
[sre]     ```
[sre]     
[sre]     Do not re-run the same tool call if a valid recall exists.
[sre]     
[sre]     ## What not to write
[sre]     
[sre]     - Do not write summaries or prose paragraphs to memory.
[sre]     - Do not write hypotheses or confidence scores.
[sre]     - Do not write tool errors (write `GAPS` in the uncertainty block instead).
[sre]     
[sre]     ## SRE-specific guidance
[sre]     
[sre]     The SRE agent's writes should cover:
[sre]     - Severity classification decisions and the evidence that triggered them
[sre]     - Escalation routing decisions (which specialist was engaged and why)
[sre]     - Time-to-first-response milestones
[sre]

[sre]     [skill:memory-protocol]
[sre]     ---
[sre]     name: memory-protocol
[sre]     description: >
[sre]       Structured episodic memory protocol for agents operating in a multi-agent
[sre]       system. Use this to write and read findings in a canonical format that
[sre]       downstream agents can reliably retrieve. Prevents duplicate tool calls and
[sre]       cross-agent correlation failures.
[sre]     metadata:
[sre]       version: "1.0.0"
[sre]       domain: sre
[sre]       tags: [memory, protocol, shared]
[sre]     ---
[sre]     
[sre]     # Memory Protocol
[sre]     
[sre]     All agents share an episodic store. Unstructured writes cannot be reliably
[sre]     retrieved downstream. Use this format for every write.
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Write format — Evidence Card
[sre]     
[sre]     Every time you write to memory, produce exactly one card per finding:
[sre]     
[sre]     ```
[sre]     MEMORY_WRITE:
[sre]       service:       <service name, e.g. payment-service>
[sre]       metric:        <what was measured, e.g. p99_latency_ms>
[sre]       value:         <observed value or range, e.g. 4200>
[sre]       timestamp:     <ISO-8601 or "from run_id=<id>">
[sre]       source_agent:  <your agent name>
[sre]       tool_call:     <tool_name(params) that produced this value>
[sre]       interpretation: <one-sentence meaning, e.g. "exceeds 2 000 ms SLO">
[sre]     ```
[sre]     
[sre]     Write multiple cards if a single tool call yields multiple distinct facts.
[sre]     Do not combine unrelated facts in one card.
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Read format — Structured Query
[sre]     
[sre]     Before calling a tool that another agent may already have run, query memory:
[sre]     
[sre]     ```
[sre]     MEMORY_READ:
[sre]       service: <service name>
[sre]       metric:  <metric name>
[sre]     ```
[sre]     
[sre]     If the store returns a match, use it and note:
[sre]     
[sre]     ```
[sre]     RECALLED: <service>/<metric> = <value> (from <source_agent>)
[sre]     ```
[sre]     
[sre]     Do not re-run the same tool call if a valid recall exists.
[sre]     
[sre]     ## What not to write
[sre]     
[sre]     - Do not write summaries or prose paragraphs to memory.
[sre]     - Do not write hypotheses or confidence scores.
[sre]     - Do not write tool errors (write `GAPS` in the uncertainty block instead).
[sre]     
[sre]     ## SRE-specific guidance
[sre]     
[sre]     The SRE agent's writes should cover:
[sre]     - Severity classification decisions and the evidence that triggered them
[sre]     - Escalation routing decisions (which specialist was engaged and why)
[sre]     - Time-to-first-response milestones
[sre]

[sre]     ---

[sre]     description: >
[sre]       Tool invocation discipline for all data-access tools (get_metrics, get_logs,
[sre]       get_service_health, get_deployments, query_db). Use this to ensure every tool
[sre]       call uses the exact canonical service name from the incident description.
[sre]       Prevents tool errors and cross-agent correlation failures.

[sre]       version: "1.0.0"

[sre]     ---
[sre]     
[sre]     # Data Access Protocol
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Tool Invocation Discipline
[sre]     
[sre]     When calling any data tool (`get_metrics`, `get_logs`, `get_service_health`,
[sre]     `get_deployments`, `query_db`), you MUST pass the canonical service name as
[sre]     the `service` argument.
[sre]     
[sre]     **Rule**: Use the **exact** service identifier from the incident description
[sre]     verbatim (e.g. `"payment-service"`). Do not omit the `service` argument, do
[sre]     not paraphrase the name, and do not substitute a generic placeholder.
[sre]     
[sre]     **Why this matters**: Omitting or misspelling the service name causes tools
[sre]     to return an error — there is no default fallback. Agents will see
[sre]     `"error": "required parameter 'service' is missing"` if the argument is
[sre]     absent. Cross-agent correlation fails when different agents query different
[sre]     service names for the same incident.
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Correct Pattern
[sre]     
[sre]     ```
[sre]     get_metrics(service="payment-service")   # ✓ exact canonical name
[sre]     get_logs(service="payment-service")      # ✓ same canonical name
[sre]     get_deployments(service="payment-service")  # ✓ consistent
[sre]     ```
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Incorrect Patterns
[sre]     
[sre]     ```
[sre]     get_metrics()                   # ✗ missing service arg → tool returns error
[sre]     get_metrics(service="payment")  # ✗ partial name → tool returns error
[sre]     get_metrics(service="service")  # ✗ generic placeholder → tool returns error
[sre]     ```
[sre]     
[sre]     ## Where to Find the Canonical Name
[sre]     
[sre]     The canonical service name appears in:
[sre]     - The incident fixture: `spec.params.incident_fixture` → `services:` keys
[sre]     - The SRE's initial incident description passed to you at delegation time
[sre]     - The incident summary in your system context

[sre]     Use it verbatim. Do not normalise underscores to hyphens or vice versa unless
[sre]     the fixture explicitly lists both as aliases.
